$comment: CANONICAL COMPONENT REGISTRY. Read this FIRST before building any UI in this repo. If a component exists here with status 'built', reuse it via its tag — never re-author the markup inline. If you need something not listed, build it as a tv-* web component, add an entry here, and add a preview section to index.html. See component-library/COMPONENTS.md.

components.name: Status tag
components.summary: ONE core chip with a fixed structure (padding, radius, optional left icon or dot, label). Two axes: tone (primary/success/warn/info/error/neutral) × variant (fill | dot). The semantic kinds (roles, member states, publication, audit events) are thin mappings onto {tone, variant, icon, label} — not separate colour definitions, so families share one tone (AI graded = Org admin = primary; adjusted = moderator = draft = warn; etc.).
useCases: Marker on a list row or canvas object (grading, members, audit entries)
Header marker inside a modal card
Member status in workspace/org settings (active / pending / deactivated)
Core use: any new chip via tone + variant, without inventing a colour

attributes.name: kind
attributes.type: moderation: ai | adjusted | flag | auto · member states: active | pending | deactivated | cancelled | expired | removed · indicators: live · roles: admin | owner | moderator | candidate | neutral · publication: draft | published | archived | coming · audit events: created | promoted | revoked
attributes.desc: Semantic shorthand — sets tone/variant/icon/label defaults from the mapping table.

attributes.name: tone
attributes.type: primary | success | warn | info | error | neutral
attributes.desc: The core colour family. Use directly to build a chip without a kind, or to override a kind.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.desc: fill = tinted bg + border + optional icon; dot = transparent with a leading status dot.

attributes.name: no-icon
attributes.desc: Suppress the icon a kind would otherwise show.

dos: Echo the same marker on the main-screen object and in the related modal header.
Pair colour with an icon/word — never colour alone.
For a new chip, pick a tone + variant — don't add a one-off colour.
donts: Don't invent new ad-hoc status pills in prototypes — add a kind mapping here instead.
Don't hardcode a new colour; map the kind onto an existing tone.

components.name: Button
components.summary: The action primitive. Used standalone and composed inside the modal card footer.
useCases: Primary / secondary actions on any surface
Destructive actions (danger variant)
Low-chrome inline actions (text variant)

attributes.name: label
attributes.desc: Text, if not using the slot.

dos: Right-align actions; secondary before primary.
Verbs lead labels (Save adjustment, Send invite).
donts: Don't restyle a raw <button> — use this so every button matches.

components.name: Diff chip
components.summary: Before → after value pair (e.g. 8 → 6) for grade changes, adjustments and audit entries. Shows a single value when there is no change.
useCases: Grade adjustment in the modal card
Audit row / audit detail summary
Any before/after value change

attributes.name: from
attributes.desc: Previous value (omit for a single value).

attributes.name: unit
attributes.desc: Small suffix on each value, e.g. /10 or %.

dos: Use inside the grade-adjust card and audit rows for consistency.
donts: Don't hand-build strike-through spans inline — use this.

components.name: Excerpt block
components.summary: Cited submission / evidence quote with a left accent border. Optional uppercase label above it.
useCases: Cited text in grade / flag cards
Justification display in audit detail
Member detail snippet (neutral accent)

attributes.name: label
attributes.desc: Optional uppercase overline above the quote.

dos: Use for any quoted/cited evidence so the accent treatment is consistent.
donts: Don't paste re-styled blockquotes inline.

components.name: Field
components.summary: Labelled form-control wrapper. Slot a native input / textarea / select inside and it gets the standard label + control styling and focus ring.
useCases: Modal card bodies (score, justification, email)
Settings edit state

attributes.name: required
attributes.desc: Shows a '— required' note by the label.

dos: Slot the control directly (input/textarea/select).
Use for all card and settings inputs so styling is uniform.
donts: Don't restyle bare inputs per-prototype.
Note: it's a visual wrapper — associate label/for yourself if you need strict a11y linkage.

components.name: Toggle switch
components.summary: On/off switch for settings rows and scoring options. Emits tv-change with the new state.
useCases: Workspace / org settings rows
Scoring options (collect a why, etc.)
dos: Use for every on/off setting so the switch is identical everywhere.
Listen for tv-change (detail.checked).
donts: Don't build bespoke switches with raw checkboxes + CSS.

components.name: Modal card
components.summary: The atom of interaction: a focused action on a single object. Header (subject + marker) and footer (destructive-left / primary-right) are fixed; only the slotted body varies. See the shared-modal-card-rulebook for when/how and the information-split rules.
useCases: Adjust a grade (with justification + diff)
Raise or dismiss a flag
Change a member's role; invite a member
View an audit entry's full before/after (read-only)

attributes.name: marker-kind / marker-label
attributes.desc: Renders a tv-status-tag in the header.

attributes.name: primary-variant
attributes.desc: Set 'danger' when the confirm action is destructive (cancel / delete / remove) — the primary button stays right but renders red.

attributes.name: danger-label
attributes.desc: Secondary destructive button (left) alongside a non-destructive primary.

attributes.name: footer-hint
attributes.desc: Optional bottom-left footer text for form modals (validation / guidance).

attributes.name: guard
attributes.desc: Prompt before closing when .dirty is true.

dos: Recognise on the screen, act in the card.
Build the body from tv-field / tv-excerpt / tv-diff.
Gate the primary with confirm-disabled until valid.
donts: Don't stack modals or open a card from a card.
Don't put deep editing or destructive actions inline on a list row.

components.name: Audit row
components.summary: Flat audit-trail entry: type marker · summary (+ optional diff) · actor · mono timestamp. Clickable — emits tv-open so the row opens the modal card for the full before/after. Composes tv-status-tag + tv-diff.
useCases: Test feedback audit trail (flat-list default)
Any change-history list that opens a detail card
components.usage: <tv-audit-row kind="adjusted" summary="Criterion 3" from="8" to="6" actor="J. Mills" time="14:22"></tv-audit-row>
dos: Use as the default flat audit list; clicking a row opens the modal card for detail.
Keep the row to recognise-at-a-glance info; full before/after lives in the card.
donts: Don't expand full detail inline on the row — that's the card's job.

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: Initials or image avatar with an optional presence ring. The single avatar used on every row, peek rail, profile header and modal-card header so they're identical everywhere.
useCases: Member / candidate rows in the Users tables
Peek rail and profile header identity
Header of a tv-modal-card acting on a person

attributes.name: name
attributes.desc: Used to derive the initials and the alt text.

attributes.name: src
attributes.desc: Image URL; falls back to initials if it fails to load.

attributes.name: status
attributes.desc: Shows a presence dot in the corner (optional).

dos: Use everywhere a person is shown so avatars are identical.
Pass name even when using src — it's the alt text and the fallback.
donts: Don't hand-roll initials divs per prototype.
Don't bake the presence dot in by hand — use status.

components.name: Metric tile
components.summary: Clickable 'platform at a glance' tile — icon + label, a big figure with optional trend, a one-line description. Extracted from system-admin-summary-v2 so the org and workspace summaries reuse the same tile. Clicking emits tv-select to open a detail card.
useCases: System / Organisation / Workspace summary metrics
Any clickable headline number that opens a tv-modal-card detail

attributes.name: metric
attributes.desc: Id echoed back in the tv-select event detail.

attributes.name: compact
attributes.desc: Smaller padding + figure for 3-up sub-tile rows.

attributes.name: accent
attributes.type: primary | purple | sky | orange | teal | success | info | colour
attributes.desc: Render the icon in a coloured tinted box (opt-in). Omit for a plain inline icon.

attributes.name: trend-pill
attributes.desc: Render the trend as a background pill (up = green, flat = grey, down = red) instead of plain coloured text.

components.usage: <tv-metric-tile metric="members" icon="users" label="Members" value="318" trend="+24 this week" arrow desc="Everyone platform-wide."></tv-metric-tile>
dos: Use one big tile + a 3-up row of compact tiles, like summary-v2.
Listen for tv-select and open a tv-modal-card detail.
donts: Don't hand-roll .ss2-tile copies — use this tile.
Don't put the detail inline; open a card.

components.name: Settings section
components.summary: A settings section that reads as calm labelled values and flips to an edit form per section on demand (state follows mode: view vs edit, not a flat wall of inputs). You slot the view and the edit form; the component owns the Edit affordance and the Cancel / Save footer. Content stays in light DOM so prototype JS can read the inputs.
useCases: Organisation settings (details, billing)
Workspace settings (name, grading model, options)
Any settings surface that should default to read and edit on demand

attributes.name: editing
attributes.desc: Reflected; present while in edit mode.

dos: Provide both a slot="view" (labelled values) and slot="edit" (the form).
Build the edit slot from tv-field / tv-toggle.
Listen for tv-save to persist + refresh the view.
donts: Don't leave every field always-editable.
Don't add your own Save button — the footer owns it.

components.name: Peek rail
components.summary: The 325px right-hand peek rail on the Users tabs. Empty by default; show a person without leaving the list — identity up top, supporting meta below, quick actions at the foot. Recognise on the rail; deep actions open a tv-modal-card. Data-driven (set .data) and composes tv-avatar + tv-status-tag.
useCases: Workspace settings Users tab peek
Organisation Users tab peek
Any list where a row should reveal detail beside it

attributes.name: open
attributes.desc: Reflected; detail vs empty. Set automatically by .data / show() / clear().

attributes.name: data
attributes.desc: Alternative to the .data property (for static markup).

components.usage: rail.data = { name:'Sarah Chen', email:'…', status:{kind:'active',label:'Active'}, tags:[{kind:'admin',label:'Org Admin'}], meta:[{label:'Job title',value:'L&D Lead'}], actions:[{id:'role',icon:'shield',label:'Change role'}] }
dos: Set one .data object instead of reaching into internals.
Route quick actions (tv-action) to a tv-modal-card.
Echo the row's status marker in the rail.
donts: Don't deep-edit inside the rail — that's the card's job.
Don't keep a permanent empty column with no close affordance.

components.name: Nav item
components.summary: The side-nav menu link atom — icon + label with the four states the rail needs: default, hover, active (indigo fill, white text) and collapsed (icon only, centred). Optional trailing count. Lifted from the dashboard `.sb-item` so every sidebar row is identical.
useCases: Rows inside a sidebar nav group
Org / workspace / system-admin navigation
Any rail link that needs an active + collapsed state

attributes.name: icon
attributes.type: layout-dashboard | layout-grid | users | settings | plug | shield | building | user | file-text | folder | credit-card | bell

attributes.name: active
attributes.desc: Current page — indigo fill, white text/icon.

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.desc: Icon only (label + count hidden, centred). Usually set by tv-sidebar.

attributes.name: count
attributes.desc: Optional trailing number chip (hidden when collapsed).

dos: Use one active item per nav group.
Pass label even when collapsed — it becomes the tooltip.
donts: Don't hand-build `.sb-item` copies inline.
Don't bake the collapsed state by hand — let tv-sidebar drive it.

components.name: Nav user button
components.summary: The bottom-pinned user profile button in the side nav. Avatar + name + chevron; clicking opens a small menu (View profile / Sign out). Composes tv-avatar. Collapses to avatar-only with the menu opening to the right. Lifted from the dashboard `.sb-user`.
useCases: Footer of the sidebar (identity + profile menu)
Any rail that needs a self-account affordance

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.desc: Avatar only; menu opens to the right. Usually set by tv-sidebar.

dos: Place in the tv-sidebar footer slot.
Route tv-action (view-profile / sign-out) to navigation / auth.
donts: Don't add a separate top-bar role chip — this is the account affordance.
Don't hand-roll the initials avatar — it composes tv-avatar.

components.name: Nav header
components.summary: The side-nav brand header — the Traverse Studio wordmark plus the collapse toggle. In the collapsed rail the wordmark hides and the toggle centres (and flips direction). Emits tv-toggle-collapse for tv-sidebar to act on. Lifted from the dashboard `.sb-brand`.
useCases: Top of the sidebar (brand + collapse control)

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.desc: Hide wordmark, centre + flip the toggle. Usually set by tv-sidebar.

dos: Place in the tv-sidebar header slot — it wires the collapse toggle automatically.
donts: Don't put navigation links in the header — those are tv-nav-items.

components.name: Nav group heading
components.summary: The small uppercase section label (eyebrow) above a group of menu links. Hides entirely in the collapsed rail. Lifted from the dashboard `.sb-eyebrow`. Usually supplied via tv-nav-group's `heading` attribute rather than placed directly.
useCases: Section label inside a tv-nav-group
Chunking a long sidebar into labelled sections

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.desc: Hidden entirely in the collapsed rail.

dos: Prefer the tv-nav-group `heading` attribute over placing this directly.
donts: Don't use it as a clickable item — it's a label only.

components.name: Nav group
components.summary: A menu list item group: an optional heading (tv-nav-heading) followed by a slotted list of tv-nav-items. Chunks the sidebar into labelled sections; tv-sidebar propagates the collapsed flag through it to the items.
useCases: A labelled block of nav items in the sidebar
Grouping primary vs settings vs admin links

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.desc: Propagates to the heading. Usually set by tv-sidebar.

dos: Slot tv-nav-items directly inside.
Use the heading attribute rather than a separate tv-nav-heading.
donts: Don't nest groups inside groups.

components.name: Sidebar
components.summary: The main side navigation. Composes the nav atoms into the full rail and owns the open ⇆ collapsed behaviour — it animates its width (240 ⇆ 64) and propagates the collapsed flag down to every slotted tv-nav-* so labels, headings and the wordmark hide together. Lifted from the dashboard `.sidebar`.
useCases: The org / workspace / system-admin left nav
Any app shell needing a collapsible rail
dos: Slot a tv-nav-header (header), groups/items (default) and a tv-nav-user (footer).
Let the header's toggle drive collapse — it's wired automatically.
donts: Don't set collapsed on each child by hand — the sidebar propagates it.
Don't fix a height inside it; give the parent shell the height.

components.name: Nav back link
components.summary: The side-nav back link at the top of a secondary rail (System Admin / Workspace / Organisation settings) that returns to the parent surface. Chevron + label; collapses to the chevron alone. Lifted from the dashboard `.sa-back`.
useCases: Top of a settings / admin sub-rail
Any rail that drills down and needs a way back up

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.desc: Icon only (label hidden, centred). Usually set by tv-sidebar.

attributes.name: href
attributes.desc: Optional link target (renders an <a> instead of a button).

dos: Place at the top of a secondary rail, above its nav group.
Route its click / tv-back to the parent surface.
donts: Don't use it as a primary nav item — it's a return affordance.
Don't hand-build `.sa-back` copies inline.

components.name: Workspace picker
components.summary: The side-nav workspace picker: a trigger row (avatar + name + optional org sub-line) opening a dropdown with a 'Switch workspace' sub-drawer and a slot for persona-conditional actions. The sub-drawer renders a flat list (normal users) or an org-grouped, searchable, A–Z-navigable list (super users). Presentational — the page feeds the workspace data in and reacts to tv-workspace-select. Lifted from the dashboard `.sb-workspace` / `.ws-dropdown` / `.ws-sub-drawer`.
useCases: Top of the workspace sidebar, under the brand header
Switching workspace within an org, or across orgs (super users)

attributes.name: ws-org
attributes.desc: Org sub-line (super users only; hidden when empty).

attributes.name: current
attributes.desc: Current workspace id — highlights its row.

attributes.name: multi
attributes.desc: User belongs to >1 workspace — shows 'Switch workspace'.

attributes.name: static
attributes.desc: Single-workspace member — row is non-interactive (no chevron, no dropdown).

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.desc: Avatar only. Usually set by tv-sidebar.

properties.name: .workspaces
properties.desc: Flat list: [{ id, name, initials, meta?, badge? }].

properties.name: .orgs
properties.desc: Grouped list: [{ org, workspaces:[{ id, name, initials, meta?, badge? }] }].

properties.name: .menuItems
properties.desc: Persona actions below the divider: [{ id, label, icon?, data?:{} }]. Rendered as real menu rows (identical to 'Switch workspace'); a click emits tv-menu-action.

dos: Feed .workspaces (or .orgs + grouped) and react to tv-workspace-select.
Provide persona actions via .menuItems and route tv-menu-action — the divider shows automatically.
Set static for a single-workspace member with no admin rights.
donts: Don't bake persona/role policy into the component — compute it in the page and feed the result in.
Don't hand-build the `.ws-dropdown` / sub-drawer markup inline.

components.name: Page header
components.summary: The standard page header on the org / workspace / system-admin pages: an uppercase overline, the page title, a description, and optional primary + secondary actions inline with the title. The two buttons are independent, so it covers both / one / no buttons. Composes tv-button. Lifted from the dashboard `.org-page-header`.
useCases: Top of any settings / list page
A titled section that needs an inline create / invite action

attributes.name: secondary-label
attributes.desc: Shows the secondary button (left of primary).

components.usage: <tv-page-header overline="Workspace" title="L&D Hub" description="Manage members…" primary-label="Add user" primary-icon="plus"></tv-page-header>
dos: Omit the button attributes for a header with no actions.
Secondary sits left of primary (the component orders them).
donts: Don't hand-roll the overline/title/sub stack inline.
Don't stack more than two header actions — overflow belongs in a menu.

components.name: Tab
components.summary: A single page tab (underline style). Optional leading icon + label + optional count, with default / hover / active / disabled states. Lifted from the dashboard `.tab`. Usually composed inside tv-tab-group, which owns the active state.
useCases: One tab in a tv-tab-group
A standalone toggle that needs the tab look

attributes.name: value
attributes.desc: Id echoed in the group's tv-change event.

attributes.name: active
attributes.desc: Current tab (indigo, underline). Usually set by tv-tab-group.

dos: Give every tab a value so the group can track it.
Let tv-tab-group own which one is active.
donts: Don't set active on more than one tab in a group.

components.name: Tab group
components.summary: The page tab strip: a row of tv-tabs with the shared bottom border. Owns the active state — clicking a tab activates it, clears the rest, and emits tv-change with the tab's value. Lifted from the dashboard `.tabs`.
useCases: Org / workspace / system-admin tab strips
Any page with switchable panels

attributes.name: value
attributes.desc: The active tab's value (reflected; read/write via .value).

dos: Set value to the initial tab.
Listen for tv-change to swap the visible panel.
donts: Don't track the active tab yourself — read tv-change / .value.

components.name: Token select
components.summary: Multi-select chip input with autocomplete. One component, two modes: mode="email" adds free-text email tokens (validated) for inviting new users; mode="options" filters a supplied list of existing users/workspaces and adds the picked ones as chips (user rows show a tv-avatar + email). Feed the list via the .options property; read the picks via .value / .selected or the tv-change event. Backbone of every invite / add-user modal.
useCases: Org invite modal — multi-email addresses + multi-workspace selection
Workspace add-user modal — add several existing org users at once
Any add-many-from-a-list or enter-many-emails field

attributes.name: mode
attributes.desc: 'email' = free-text validated email tokens; 'options' = pick from .options with autocomplete.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.desc: Input placeholder, shown while no chips are selected.

dos: Feed existing users/workspaces via .options after the element upgrades (customElements.whenDefined('tv-token-select')).
Read picks via .value / tv-change, not by scraping chips.
Use mode="email" only where genuinely new users are provisioned (org-level invite).
donts: Don't use mode="email" for workspace add-user — workspaces add existing org users only.
Don't rebuild a chip/autocomplete inline — extend this component.

components.name: Start step
components.summary: One step in a guided get-started / onboarding path: a numbered row with an icon tile, title, one-line description and a trailing action. Three states carry 'what's available to you' — todo (actionable button), done (muted + green check), locked (prerequisite not met, action disabled with a lock). Stack several to form an empty-state setup path. Composes tv-button; emits tv-action on the CTA.
useCases: Empty-workspace get-started path (simulation → assessment → test → invite)
First-run setup checklist where later steps depend on earlier ones
Progress-aware onboarding that doubles as an availability tracker

attributes.name: number
attributes.desc: Sequence label, rendered as 'Step N'. Optional.

attributes.name: icon
attributes.desc: Leading Lucide icon for the tile (overridden by check/lock in done/locked states).

attributes.name: variant
attributes.desc: Button style — use primary for the current next action.

attributes.name: status
attributes.desc: todo = actionable; done = muted + check, no button; locked = disabled action + lock tile.

components.usage: <tv-start-step number="1" icon="film" variant="primary" title="Create a simulation" desc="Build the scenario candidates work through." cta="Create simulation"></tv-start-step>
dos: Give the current next action variant="primary"; leave the rest secondary.
Mark steps whose prerequisites don't exist yet as status="locked".
Listen for tv-action to open the matching create flow.
donts: Don't hand-roll onboarding rows inline — stack these.
Don't leave every step primary — only the next actionable one.

components.name: Create tile
components.summary: A compact 'create X' tile: entity icon, label, and a plus affordance. Used in empty-state / get-started hubs where an author launches a create flow for a content type or workspace building block. Clicking emits tv-action; supports a disabled state.
useCases: Workspace-admin first-run hub (create environments/templates/characters + assessments/tests/simulations/sequences)
Any empty-state grid of 'create <type>' launch points

attributes.name: desc
attributes.desc: Optional one-line hint under the label (always shown when featured).

attributes.name: accent
attributes.desc: Family colour for the icon box (indigo|purple|sky|teal|green|orange|pink|red|yellow|grey), tinted via color-mix. Omit for the neutral grey box.

attributes.name: featured
attributes.desc: Flagship treatment: larger padding, 48px icon box, title at tv-h5, description always shown. For the hero create tile in a hub.

components.usage:
<tv-create-tile icon="film" label="Simulation"></tv-create-tile>
<tv-create-tile featured accent="sky" icon="film" label="Simulation" desc="An interactive scenario a candidate works through."></tv-create-tile>
dos: Group tiles by the level they live on (workspace building blocks vs content pieces).
Use featured + accent for the flagship of a group (e.g. Simulation, Assessment); plain tiles for supporting building blocks.
Listen for tv-action to open the matching create flow.
donts: Don't use for a primary single action — that's a tv-button or tv-start-step.
Don't hand-roll create cards inline.

components.name: Path card
components.summary: A large, selectable 'choose your path' card for a first-run chooser (e.g. 'What are you setting up — Simulations or Assessments?'). Family-accented icon tile (or a row of sanctioned illustration thumbnails), a title, a purpose line, and a selected state. Clicking emits tv-select; the parent manages single-select.
useCases: First-run dashboard path chooser (Simulations vs Assessments) with progressive disclosure
Any two-or-three-way 'pick a setup track' fork at the top of an empty state

attributes.name: value
attributes.desc: Identifier returned in the tv-select detail.

attributes.name: icon
attributes.desc: Leading Lucide icon (used when no images given).

attributes.name: accent
attributes.desc: Family colour for the icon box (indigo|purple|sky|teal|green|orange|pink|red|yellow|grey).

attributes.name: images
attributes.desc: Optional comma-separated image srcs (sanctioned illustrations, e.g. sim-icon PNGs) shown instead of the icon box.

attributes.name: selected
attributes.desc: Reflected chosen state: primary border + primary-50 tint + check.

components.usage: <tv-path-card value="simulations" accent="sky" icon="film" label="Simulations" desc="Build interactive scenarios candidates work through."></tv-path-card>
dos: Use in a small group (2–3) as the top-level fork of a first-run flow.
Manage selection in the parent: mark the chosen card selected and clear the others on tv-select.
Use images only for sanctioned illustrations (sim-icon PNGs) — never redraw as SVG.
donts: Don't use for a routine create action — that's a tv-create-tile.
Don't rely on the component to enforce single-select; the parent owns that.

components.name: Guided tour
components.summary: A step-through onboarding tour. Walks a set of 'pieces' one at a time, top of hierarchy → smallest parts: each step names its tier, says plainly what the piece is, shows its sub-parts as chips, and offers the matching create action. Progress dots, Back / Next / Skip. Learning ties straight to doing.
useCases: First-run dashboard: teach the content model (Environment → Simulation/Test/Content → Assessment/Sequence) before the author builds
Any first-use walkthrough of a nested concept where each step maps to an action

attributes.name: steps
attributes.desc: Set in JS (not an attribute): array of { tier, icon, accent, title, body, chips?, cta?, ctaValue? }. accent maps to a --cat-* family. A step with cta shows a primary/secondary action button that emits tv-action.

components.usage:
<tv-guided-tour id="tour"></tv-guided-tour>
<script>customElements.whenDefined('tv-guided-tour').then(function(){document.getElementById('tour').steps=[{tier:'Foundation',icon:'box',accent:'teal',title:'Environment',body:'The world your content is built in…',chips:['Characters','Terms','Tone'],cta:'Create environment',ctaValue:'environment'}]})</script>
dos: Order steps top of hierarchy → smallest pieces so the tour teaches the model's shape.
Give each step a cta that maps to the real create flow, so learning ties to doing.
Reset() when the tour is re-opened so it starts on step 1.
donts: Don't use for a persistent action surface — that's a grid of tv-create-tile / tv-start-step.
Don't cram more than a short chip list per step; the tour is a primer, not a spec.

components.name: Priority actions
components.summary: A role-adaptive strip of the most-important actions, ordered by importance. The first action gets primary emphasis (the single most-important thing this role does); the rest follow as supporting actions. Used at the top of a dashboard so each role leads with the right next step.
useCases: Role-adaptive dashboard header — Admin leads with Configure/Manage users; Member with Create content; Moderator with Grade submissions; Viewer with View content
Any surface that should present a small, ordered set of primary next actions

attributes.name: heading
attributes.desc: Optional overline shown above the actions.

attributes.name: actions
attributes.desc: Set in JS (not an attribute): array of { icon, accent, label, desc?, value }, most-important first. accent maps to a --cat-* family. The first item renders with primary emphasis.

components.usage:
<tv-priority-actions id="pa" heading="Your priorities"></tv-priority-actions>
<script>customElements.whenDefined('tv-priority-actions').then(function(){document.getElementById('pa').actions=[{icon:'settings',accent:'indigo',label:'Configure workspace',desc:'Grading model, branding and integrations.',value:'configure'},{icon:'users',accent:'teal',label:'Manage users',desc:'Invite people and assign roles.',value:'users'}]})</script>
dos: Order actions by real importance for the role — the first is rendered as the primary action.
Keep it to 3–4 actions; it's a lead-with strip, not a full menu.
Route tv-action values to the matching screen or flow.
donts: Don't show actions the role can't perform — hide them (per the RBAC UI rules).
Don't use for a long list of links; that's navigation, not priorities.

components.name: Quick actions
components.summary: A persistent right-rail panel of the role's most-important actions. Sits in the same 325px sticky rail as tv-peek-rail: a titled panel of full-width action cards, each with an accent icon, label, optional description, and an up-right (↗) arrow in the top-right corner. Always visible so key actions are immediately findable and one click to fire.
useCases: The quick-actions rail on the active role dashboards (Admin / Member / Moderator / Viewer)
Any two-pane surface that wants an always-visible column of primary next actions

attributes.name: actions
attributes.desc: Set in JS (not an attribute): array of { icon, accent, label, desc?, value }. accent maps to a --cat-* family. Each item renders as a full-width card with a top-right ↗ arrow.

components.usage:
<tv-quick-actions id="qa" heading="Quick actions"></tv-quick-actions>
<script>customElements.whenDefined('tv-quick-actions').then(function(){document.getElementById('qa').actions=[{icon:'file-text',accent:'indigo',label:'Review feedback',desc:'11 candidates waiting for approval.',value:'review-feedback'},{icon:'user-plus',accent:'teal',label:'Invite users',value:'invite'}]})</script>
dos: Use it as the always-on rail beside the main dashboard column (same slot as tv-peek-rail).
Feed 2–5 role-appropriate actions, most-important first.
Route tv-action values to the matching screen or flow.
donts: Don't show actions the role can't perform — hide them (per the RBAC UI rules).
Don't stuff it with navigation links; it's for priority actions, not a menu.

components.name: Setup stepper
components.summary: A compact, selectable vertical stepper for a guided setup: a connected list of steps, each showing a completed / current / upcoming state. Clicking a step selects it (the parent swaps the working canvas beside it). Completed steps show a check; the current step is highlighted.
useCases: The stepper column of a stepper + working-canvas onboarding layout (e.g. the Org Owner landing)
Any guided multi-step setup where progress and current-step state matter

attributes.name: steps
attributes.desc: Set in JS: array of { id, title, status:'done'|'current'|'upcoming', note? }. note overrides the default state label (e.g. 'Coming soon').

dos: Pair it with a working canvas the parent swaps on tv-step-select.
Keep step titles short; the state label carries the status.
Update statuses (done/current/upcoming) as the user completes steps.
donts: Don't put form fields in the stepper — those belong in the canvas beside it.
Don't use for navigation between unrelated pages.

components.name: Build card
components.summary: A 'starting point' card: an icon + title, an abstract placeholder graphic that illustrates the task type, a one-line description, and a primary action. Used in a grid of role-specific get-started launch points. The graphic is a token-built skeleton (rectangles, lines, dots) — not an illustrated character or hand-drawn art — so it stays inside the design-system rules.
useCases: Role-specific 'what to set up / build next' grids (Org Owner: add workspace / invite users; Member: simulation / grading / content)
Any get-started launch grid where a visual hint of the task type helps

attributes.name: accent
attributes.desc: --cat-* family for the icon tile and graphic tints.

attributes.name: graphic
attributes.desc: Placeholder skeleton variant: workspaces | users | settings | chart | simulation | grading | content | templates | environment. The graphic frame carries a faint accent wash.

attributes.name: featured
attributes.desc: Larger emphasis: primary border + primary CTA.

components.usage: <tv-build-card icon="layout-grid" accent="sky" graphic="workspaces" title="Add a workspace" desc="Create a space for a team or department." value="add-workspace"></tv-build-card>
dos: Use graphic to hint the task type; keep to the built-in token skeletons.
Feature the one or two core-focus cards for the role; leave the rest plain.
Route tv-action value to the matching create flow.
donts: Don't swap the skeleton for a hand-drawn or character illustration.
Don't use for a routine inline action — that's a tv-create-tile or tv-button.

components.name: Resource rail
components.summary: A slim right-hand rail that lists resources or helpful tips as tappable rows (icon · title · optional one-liner · chevron). Sits beside a working area to offer guidance without taking the reader out of the flow. Optional heading and an emphasised footer row (e.g. 'Book a call').
useCases: The resources/tips column beside a stepper + working-canvas setup layout
Any slim contextual help rail alongside a task surface

attributes.name: items
attributes.desc: Set in JS: array of { icon, title, desc?, value } rendered as rows.

attributes.name: footer
attributes.desc: Set in JS: optional { icon, title, desc?, value } emphasised row at the foot.

components.usage:
<tv-resource-rail id="rail" heading="Resources & tips"></tv-resource-rail>
<script>customElements.whenDefined('tv-resource-rail').then(function(){document.getElementById('rail').items=[{icon:'book-open',title:'How organisations work',desc:'The org → workspace model.',value:'orgs'}]})</script>
dos: Keep titles short; use desc for a one-line hint only.
Use footer for a single stand-out action like booking a call.
Route tv-action value to the matching resource or flow.
donts: Don't use it as the primary content column — it's a supporting rail.
Don't overload it; a handful of rows keeps it scannable.

components.name: Launch tile
components.summary: A launchpad tile: an accent icon, a title, a supporting line and a trailing arrow — the whole tile is the action. Used to build role-adaptive dashboard 'launchpad' grids: core actions for a role and entry points into core platform areas. Elevation + an optional accent tint give the grid layers and colour instead of flat white cards.
useCases: The 'Start here' core-action grid on a role's launchpad (featured tiles)
The 'Explore' core-platform-area grid (tinted, colourful tiles with a count)

attributes.name: accent
attributes.desc: --cat-* family for the icon, tint and hover arrow.

attributes.name: meta
attributes.desc: Small accent-coloured footer label (e.g. a count or 'Coming soon').

attributes.name: featured
attributes.desc: Larger + more elevated, for primary core actions.

attributes.name: tint
attributes.desc: Accent-washed background + accent border, for a colourful area tile.

components.usage:
<tv-launch-tile featured icon="settings" accent="indigo" title="Set up your organisation" desc="Branding, authentication and billing." value="setup"></tv-launch-tile>
<tv-launch-tile tint icon="layout-grid" accent="sky" meta="1 workspace" title="Workspaces" desc="Spaces for teams to work in." value="workspaces"></tv-launch-tile>
dos: Use featured for the small set of core actions; use tint for the colourful area grid.
Give area tiles a meta count so the grid reads as live, not empty.
Vary the accent across area tiles for colour and scannability.
donts: Don't put a separate CTA button inside — the whole tile is the action.
Don't mix flat (untinted, unfeatured) tiles into a tinted area grid; keep a grid consistent.

components.name: Setup checklist
components.summary: A condensed setup card: a short list of get-started actions, each on one line — icon, label, an inline progress/status indicator, and an action button. An item can be in progress (mini bar + percent), todo (just the button), or done (a check, no button). Small and dismissible — designed to sit inside a welcome banner.
useCases: The condensed setup card baked into a role's welcome banner (org owner: set up org, add workspace, invite users)
Any compact 'finish setting up' list where each item has a state and one action

attributes.name: heading
attributes.desc: Optional overline; a 'N of M done' count shows opposite it.

attributes.name: items
attributes.desc: Set in JS: array of { icon, label, status:'todo'|'in-progress'|'done', progress?, cta?, value }. in-progress shows a mini bar + percent; done shows a check and no button.

components.usage:
<tv-setup-checklist id="setup" heading="Finish setting up"></tv-setup-checklist>
<script>customElements.whenDefined('tv-setup-checklist').then(function(){document.getElementById('setup').items=[{icon:'building-2',label:'Set up your organisation',status:'in-progress',progress:33,cta:'Setup organisation',value:'setup-org'},{icon:'layout-grid',label:'Add your first workspace',status:'todo',cta:'Add workspace',value:'add-workspace'}]})</script>
dos: Keep it to a few items; it's a nudge, not the whole page.
Use in-progress + progress to show momentum on multi-part steps.
Put it inside a dismissible welcome banner so the two dismiss together.
donts: Don't use it as a full working surface — it launches flows, it isn't one.
Don't add per-item descriptions; keep each row to a single line.
